## 5. Capacity and placement as a performance factor (live numbers, 2026-10-02 17:46-18:00 UTC)

### 5.1 Current state per node

| | N1 primary (SGP) | N2 (FSN) | N3 (SGP) | N4 (SGP) | N5 (BHS) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| CPU | i7-7700K 4C/8T | i7-8700 6C/12T | Xeon E-2236 6C/12T | i7-7700K 4C/8T | Xeon E-2136 6C/12T |
| Physical RAM | 64 GB | 64 GB | **32 GB** | 64 GB | 64 GB |
| Running VMs / vCPU / vCPU per thread | 13 / 32 / **4.0** | 12 / 27 / 2.3 | 6 / 13 / 1.1 | 17 / 37 / **4.6** | 8 / 16 / 1.3 |
| Sum of running VM RAM ("ceiling") / physical | 66.0 GB = **103%** | 67.6 GB = **106%** | 28.7 GB = 90% (+8.5 GB ARC on 32 GB) | 77.8 GB = **122%** | 30.7 GB = 48% |
| DB committed (plan RAM) vs `Node.capacityRamMB` | 43.0 / 56.0 GB = 77% | 67.6 / 56.2 = **120%** | 28.7 / 23.9 = **120%** | 75.8 / 56.0 = **135%** | 26.6 / 56.1 = 47% |
| Host MemAvailable | 16 GB | 14 GB | **3.3 GB** | **1.9 GB** | 25 GB |
| Host swap used | **10.2 / 10.2 GB (full)** | none | 1.5 / 2 GB | **2.0 / 2.0 GB (full)** | 0 |
| Guest memory actually in use (balloon stats) vs paid | 32.7 / 65.5 GB (50%) | 31.9 / 67.6 (47%) | 12.6 / 28.7 (44%) | 44.2 / 77.8 (57%) | 21.0 / 30.7 (68%) |
| Customer VMs currently ballooned below paid RAM | **9 VMs, 11.0 GB** (e.g. 5.6 of 8 GB, 4.4 of 6 GB) | 1 VM, 0.9 GB | **5 VMs, 12.3 GB (each at 50%)** | **3 VMs, 6.1 GB (each at 50%)** | 0 |
| CPU PSI (some, avg60 / avg300) | **49% / 36%** | 0 | 0 | 4% / 3.4% | 0 |
| ARC (max / size / hit ratio) | 8 GB / 4.3 / 91% | **0.4 GB** / 0.38 / 87% | 8 / 8.6 / 95% | 8 / **2.1 (starved)** / 94% | 8 / 8.3 / 92% |
| VM pool used / sold virtual disk | 68% (246/358 GB) / 733 GB = **2.0x** | 23% / 620 GB on 472 GB | 19% / 280 GB on 928 GB | **65% (261/396 GB)** / 994 GB = **2.5x** | 16% / 200 GB on 452 GB |
| Accepts new provisions (`acceptsProvisions`) | **no** | yes | **no** | yes | yes |
| Uplink | 1 Gb | 1 Gb | 1 Gb link | 1 Gb | 10 Gb |

Notes and caveats:
- Steal time is not applicable (bare metal hosts, `steal` 0 in `/proc/stat`). The noisy-neighbour signal on these hosts is **host CPU PSI, run-queue and swap**, not steal: only N1 (and mildly N4) show CPU contention; N1 also runs the Nxeon app, Postgres and `next build` (see `docs/PRIMARY-OFFLOAD-PLAN.md`, still valid: load 20 on 8 threads at sampling time).
- "Guest memory in use" is the guest balloon stat; qemu RSS is larger (page cache, never-returned pages). With pinned RAM the host cost of a VM trends toward its full ceiling as the guest touches pages, which is why a 122% ceiling on N4 already produces full swap with 1.9 GB free.
- Ballooning: new VMs are pinned (`balloon = memory`, `NXEON_BALLOON_POLICY` default `pin`), but **17 running VMs still sit at the old 50% floor and are currently squeezed**, including N1 vm 105 (live Soul Pilates) at 5.6/8 GB. Re-pinning them without first adding capacity would push N3/N4/N1 into OOM. The `perf-hypervisor.md` P0-2 recommendation is right but must come **after** R7.
- "Germany/Canada have room" is only half true: **N5 (Canada) really has room** (47% committed, 25 GB free). **N2 (Germany) is also over-committed** by the platform's own accounting (120%, ceiling 106% of physical) although its real use (47%) and 14 GB free look comfortable. Capacity numbers in `Node.capacityRamMB` are also stale (N3 is a 32 GB box configured as 23.9 GB, which is conservative; N4 is a 64 GB box configured as 56 GB).
- `NXEON_RAM_GUARD` defaults to `warn` (log only) because enforcing it refused every Singapore order on 10-01; the scheduler's real rule is DB plan-RAM under 90% critical for strict (region-bound) placement. It is **RAM only: no CPU, no live PSI, no swap, no disk-overcommit, no template/cache locality.**

### 5.2 How oversubscribed, in sellable terms

Policy used by the existing guard: guaranteed RAM <= 0.95 x (physical - 10 GB host reserve) = 51.3 GB on a 64 GB node, 20.9 GB on N3.

| Node | Pinned/ceiling RAM now | Allowed | Over (GB) |
|---|---|---|---|
| N1 | 66.0 | 51.3 | +14.7 (includes ~15.7 GB of company VMs: mail, hosting, studio) |
| N2 | 67.6 | 51.3 | +16.3 |
| N3 | 28.7 | 20.9 | +7.8 |
| N4 | 77.8 | 51.3 | +26.5 |
| N5 | 30.7 | 51.3 | **-20.6 (headroom)** |

The fleet is **~65 GB over the policy line against ~21 GB of headroom, all of it in Canada**. In Singapore (the region taking ~61% of new orders, see below) there is **no** sellable headroom at all and nothing can be re-pinned. Real usage is only ~53% of paid RAM fleet-wide (142 of 270 GB), so the situation is not an imminent mass-OOM, but N4 (1.9 GB free, swap full) and N3 (3.3 GB free) are one burst away, and N1 already had an OOM kill of the mail VM on 2026-09-25 (per `perf-hypervisor.md`).

### 5.3 Demand (from the DB)

- 52 live servers, **44 created in the last 30 days**, 17 in the last 7. By region (30 d): Singapore 27 servers / 123 GB plan RAM, Germany 10 / 54 GB, Canada 7 / 26 GB. Singapore 7-day: 8 servers / 32 GB (~4.5 GB/day). At that rate **one 64 GB node's ~51 GB of sellable RAM lasts ~11-12 days in Singapore**. (Uncertainty: the window may include partner grants, tests and a launch spike; I did not separate them.)
- Order mix: games 33 of 44 (Minecraft first), plain VPS 11.

### 5.4 Recommended placement and overcommit policy

1. **No overcommit of pinned RAM for game servers.** Sum of guaranteed RAM <= 0.95 x (RAM - 12 GB) per node, enforced (`NXEON_RAM_GUARD=enforce`) once R7's new node exists; until then keep `warn` and rely on `acceptsProvisions=false` on full nodes. Never balloon a game VM below plan RAM.
2. **Optional measured overcommit for plain VPS only**, after a month of per-VM RSS data: idle VPS use 25-45% of RAM (e.g. VMs 102/104/108 etc. in the cap data), so a ceiling-to-physical ratio of up to ~1.15 could be defensible *if* free-page reporting is verified; do not do this on nodes with ARC starved or swap in use.
3. **Schedule on live signals, not just DB plan-RAM**: reject or penalise a node when MemAvailable < 10%, swap > 25% used, CPU PSI some avg300 > 15-20%, vCPU:thread > 3:1 (N1 4.0, N4 4.6 today), pool > 75% used (ZFS degrades past ~80%; N4 65% with 2.5x sold) or sold-virtual > 2x pool.
4. **Prefer a node that already holds the golden/game-file template and image cache** for the family, then most sellable headroom.
5. **Stop N1 taking customer load** (already `acceptsProvisions=false`; the offload plan stands). Keep N3 closed until its ARC (8.5 GB on 32 GB) is cut to ~3 GB and RAM is re-based (it is the weakest box: 32 GB).
6. Fix `Node.capacityRamMB` to physical RAM minus reserve per node so DB capacity and the guard agree; add per-node `capacityVcpu` (suggest <= 3:1 per thread for game nodes, as game servers are single-thread bound and N1/N4 show contention).

### 5.5 Capacity plan: when and what

Triggers to order a node (any one): sellable headroom in a region < 2 weeks of recent demand (Singapore today: **0 days, trigger already tripped**); host MemAvailable < 10% for 1 h; swap used > 25%; CPU PSI some avg300 > 20%; pool used > 75% or sold virtual > 2x; ARC cannot reach its target.

Spec: the existing boxes are RAM-bound, not CPU-bound (CPU PSI 0 everywhere except N1), and VM RAM is what is sold, so buy **RAM per node**: **12-16 threads, 128 GB ECC, 2 x NVMe >= 960 GB mirror (pools are 358-452 GB today and 2.0-2.5x sold on N1/N4), 10 GbE if offered (Steam installs, 1 Gb is shared by every simultaneous install)**. A 128 GB node sells ~108 GB (0.95 x (128-12)... conservative 100 GB), i.e. ~3 weeks of Singapore demand at the recent rate. Order **two Singapore nodes** (one is already needed to un-squeeze N1/N3/N4 and re-pin 17 VMs; the second covers growth and gives N+1 so a node can be drained for maintenance). Cost reference from the DB: current nodes cost $33-78/month each (`monthlyCostCents`); I have no price for a 128 GB class, so no cost claim. Order lead time is the risk: place the order before the next campaign, not after.

Other capacity-adjacent findings worth flagging: N5's `backup`/`vmdata-hdd` is a **20 GB directory at 90.7% used** (backups for node-5 servers will fail soon); N2's NVMe pair and N5's second NVMe have high wear per `perf-hypervisor.md`; N1 root disk was 98% full on 10-01 (Postgres crash 09-27).

---

## 6. Rollout, canary and measurement

Common rule: **N5 is the canary node** (healthy, 10 Gb, 47% committed, accepts provisions), then N3/N2, then N4. Template presence per node is already the natural per-node switch (`chooseCloneSource` falls back to stock if the template is missing), which gives instant rollback (untag or remove the template; no deploy).

| Step | Do | Verify | Roll back |
|---|---|---|---|
| R0 | Add `Job.phases`; record: claimed, inventory done, clone done, config done, started, agent up, ssh up, login ok, game stage start, port open, readiness done, DONE; add `Server.cloneSource` (vmid, golden flag) | 10 real provisions show all marks; admin table of p50/p90 per family/node/cloneSource | Column is additive; ignore it |
| R1 | Build `base` Ubuntu 24.04 template on N5 (new vmid in 9100-9199, run the existing build script with no images); allow `chooseCloneSource` for non-game Ubuntu 24.04 | 5 canary VPS orders on N5: agent up <= 25 s, total <= 90 s; SSH login, password and management key work; `cloud-init status` clean; no `package_update` in the log | Remove the template from N5 |
| R2 | Rebuild `game-base` at 9-10 G with the top image set; set `NXEON_GOLDEN_GAME_TEMPLATE` + `NXEON_GOLDEN_LINKED_CLONE=1` (or the DB mapping); N5 only | 5 Minecraft + 3 Terraria/Core Keeper + 2 Valheim on N5; `scripts/verify-game-provision.ts` `CLEAN BILL OF HEALTH`; compare p50 with the baselines in 2.1/2.3; test a **backup, restore and VM move of a linked-clone server** on a scratch VM before opening it to customers | Unset env / remove template; existing servers are unaffected (their disks are independent or tied only to their own old template snapshot) |
| R3 | Run `registry:2` proxy on N2 first; per-node mirror setting | A provision on N2 shows pulls hitting the cache (cache logs); a stopped cache still provisions | Clear the mirror setting |
| R4 | One family at a time (Valheim first, highest volume among Steam families) on N5 | Install time and `verify-game-provision` identical to a cold install; no world/secret in the template (diff the template's `/opt` against a clean image) | Remove template |
| R7 | Order nodes; onboard with `scripts/onboard-node.sh` (it already sets ARC cap, firewall, agent, templates from archives); then re-pin the 17 squeezed VMs and flip `NXEON_RAM_GUARD=enforce` | MemAvailable, swap, CPU PSI per node before/after | n/a |

Metrics to track from R0 on (per family and per node): p50/p90 claim-to-RUNNING, first-attempt success rate, % of jobs needing a retry, and the per-phase table; node-side: MemAvailable, swap used, CPU PSI avg300, pool %, sold-virtual ratio. Success criteria: plain VPS p50 <= 75 s, Minecraft/Terraria/Core Keeper p50 <= 120 s, first-attempt success >= 90% on games, 0 customer VMs below plan RAM.

---

## 7. Uncertainty and what I did not verify

- Phase split inside the guest is inferred, not measured on these runs (no per-phase data exists). The ~50 s unexplained gap on plain Ubuntu (148-151 s from start vs ~95 s to agent-up) and the 119-147 s game stages for Terraria/Core Keeper are open until R0 exists.
- All "expected gains" for R2/R4/R6 are estimates built from measured components; only the golden POC's agent time (15 s), docker (+1.2 s) and linked clone (2.1 s) were measured, once, on N2.
- I did not run or time any provision, any clone, any `docker pull` or any Steam download; registry sizes are compressed layer sums from the Docker Hub API (amd64), not measured pull speeds. Steam install sizes are taken from the repo's docs and the sibling report.
- Linked-clone behaviour with `vzdump`, `zfs send` VM moves and `qmrestore` is reasoned from the docs/code, **not tested**.
- Whether `registry-mirrors` plus `proxy.ttl` behaves as described for `:latest` tags is from registry documentation, not tested here.
- Capacity: one snapshot at ~17:50 UTC on a Friday; no time series, no peak-hour data. The demand rate may include partner grants and tests.
- The 122 jobs without a live server were treated as test/sweep/deleted, based on the 10-01 sweep dates and error text; I did not read their server rows (deleted).
- No customer data was read; guest-internal timings for customer VMs were not collected by me (I used the existing docs and the sibling report instead).

**Evidence limits**
- No per-phase timing is stored anywhere. `Job` keeps only the last step label, and `startedAt` exists only since 2026-10-01.
- Phase timings in the report are derived from three sources: worker journal markers, Proxmox task logs on the nodes, and in-guest numbers from the repo docs and the sibling reports (`/root/research/perf-hypervisor.md` and `perf-guest-and-games.md`).
- The split inside the guest (docker install, pull, game start) is inferred, not measured.
- Of 185 PROVISION rows in 60 days, 122 have no surviving server. 81 of those are the 10-01 all-families sweep, so I excluded them. 63 jobs are usable.

**Measured baseline (provisions on stock templates, 10-02 after the guest-agent fix)**

| Type | Run time |
|---|---|
| Ubuntu VPS | 163-167 s |
| Minecraft | 251 s |
| Terraria | 285 s |
| Core Keeper | 255 s |
| Valheim | 395 s (10-01, node-4) |
| ARK | 1269 s |
| Rust | 1015-1475 s |

- Across the 63 real jobs, 19% failed and 75% succeeded on the first attempt. Plain VPS first-attempt success is 95%, games 66%.
- Almost all failures were bugs that are now fixed or known-unsellable games. The cost is the retry multiplier of 3 attempts, each with a 300 s port window.
- The Proxmox and worker side is only about 15-18 s of each provision. Clone takes a median of 8 s on the stock template.
- About 85-90% of the time is inside the guest. That includes a 72 s `package_update` on every first boot, because the stock template has no guest agent.

**Biggest findings**
- The golden-template and registry-mirror code already exists but is not enabled in prod. I checked the worker's environment: `NXEON_GOLDEN_GAME_TEMPLATE`, `NXEON_GOLDEN_LINKED_CLONE` and `NXEON_DOCKER_REGISTRY_MIRROR` are all unset.
  - Only node-2 has a proof-of-concept golden template (9101).
  - That template is 12 GB, so it excludes game plans with a disk of 5-10 GB.
  - Plain VPS orders can never use a baked template.
- Docker images are small, 150-1240 MB compressed. The real cost is Steam game files: Valheim 2.1 GB, Project Zomboid 6.9 GB, ARK 22.9 GB, Squad 21.4 GB, CS2 66-71 GB.
- Templates have drifted. All five nodes have a different ZFS guid for template 9000, and the base-image dates run from 2026-07-23 to 2026-09-29. Node-2 and node-4 lack templates 9005-9009, and node-5 also lacks 9001.
- Capacity is worse than "Singapore nearly full":
  - Pinned or ceiling RAM is 103% of physical on the primary, 106% on node-2, 122% on node-4 and 90% on node-3. Node-5 is at 48%.
  - The primary and node-4 swap are full, and node-4 has 1.9 GB free.
  - 17 running customer VMs are still ballooned below their paid RAM, up to 50% on node-3 and node-4.
  - The fleet is about 65 GB over the sellable-RAM policy line, with about 21 GB of headroom, all in Canada.
  - Germany is also over-committed (DB 120%).
  - Singapore, about 61% of new orders, has no sellable headroom. One 64 GB node there lasts roughly 11-12 days at the recent rate, though that rate may include partner grants and tests.
- Node-2's ZFS ARC is capped at 390 MB, which fits its slow clones (13-25 s vs 4-8 s elsewhere).
- Node-5's backup directory is a 20 GB directory at 90.7% used.

**Roadmap order**
1. R0: add per-phase timestamps.
2. R1: a baked Ubuntu base template with the guest agent, for plain VPS. Expected saving is about 70-100 s per provision.
3. R2: enable golden templates with linked clones, rebuilt at 9-10 GB. Expected 130-170 s saved on games.
4. R7: add Singapore nodes (a 128 GB class is suggested). This has a lead time, so it should run in parallel with the others.
5. R3: per-node registry cache.
6. R4: Steam game-file templates for Valheim, Project Zomboid, Rust, Palworld and ARK.
7. R5: raise node-2's ARC cap.
8. R6: parallelise and trim the NAT syncs (about 15-25 s).
9. R8: template drift sweep.
10. R9: warm pool, probably not worth it.

Canary is node-5 first, because template presence per node is the natural switch.

**Estimates and untested items**
- Expected gains for R2, R4 and R6 are estimates built from measured components. Only the proof-of-concept's guest-agent (15 s), docker (+1.2 s) and linked-clone (2.1 s) times were measured, once.
- I did not test linked clones against vzdump, `zfs send` moves or restore. Do that on a scratch VM before relying on it.
- About 50 s of plain-Ubuntu provisioning, and 119-147 s of game-stage time for Terraria and Core Keeper, remain unexplained until R0 exists.

Node-5 is the canary for each step, because a node uses a template only if it has one. Each step has its verify and rollback in the report.

The expected gains for R2, R4 and R6 are estimates built from measured pieces. Only the proof-of-concept's guest-agent (15 s), docker (+1.2 s) and linked-clone (2.1 s) times were measured, once. I did not test linked clones against `vzdump`, `zfs send` VM moves or restore, so test that on a scratch VM first. About 50 s of plain-Ubuntu provisioning, and 119-147 s of Terraria and Core Keeper game-stage time, stay unexplained until R0 exists.
